questions.statement: I ________ a marathon last year, and since then, I ________ to stay fit.
questions.context: Talking about a personal achievement in sports.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Last year" requires Past Simple, and the ongoing effort requires Present Perfect.
Correct! Past Simple for a finished time ("last year") and Present Perfect for an action continuing to the present.
Incorrect. These are simple present forms, not suitable for past events or ongoing results.
Incorrect. "Last year" cannot be used with Present Perfect in this context.

questions.explanation:
Usamos el *Past Simple* (*ran*) para acciones completadas en un tiempo específico del pasado (*last year*). El *Present Perfect* (*have tried*) se usa para acciones que comenzaron en el pasado y tienen relevancia o continúan en el presente.

questions.statement:
"________ you ever ________ a vegetarian diet?"
"Yes, I ________ it for a month in 2022."
questions.context: Asking about past experiences without a specific time.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Ever" usually takes Present Perfect, and "in 2022" requires Past Simple.
Correct! Present Perfect for experiences (*ever*) and Past Simple for a specific date (*in 2022*).
Incorrect. "In 2022" is a finished time, so we cannot use Present Perfect.
Incorrect. The first part is about experience, not a general habit.

questions.explanation:
Para preguntar sobre experiencias de vida en general usamos *Present Perfect* con *ever*. Sin embargo, si mencionamos un momento específico en el pasado (*in 2022*), debemos cambiar a *Past Simple*.

questions.statement: The Colombian government ________ several health campaigns since the beginning of the decade.
questions.context: Discussing the history of public health in Colombia.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Since" indicates a period starting in the past and continuing to now, requiring Present Perfect.
Correct! Present Perfect fits the timeframe starting "since the beginning of the decade".
Incorrect. This describes an action in progress in the past.
Incorrect. This is for general routines or facts.

questions.explanation:
La palabra *since* es un marcador clave del *Present Perfect*, ya que conecta el inicio de una acción en el pasado con el momento actual.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Maria ________ to the gym regularly three years ago, but she ________ a member of a yoga club for the last six months.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Three years ago" requires Past Simple.
Correct! Past Simple for the finished habit and Present Perfect for the current situation.
Incorrect. Doesn't correctly reflect the past time markers.
Incorrect. "For the last six months" implies she is still a member.

questions.explanation:
Diferenciamos entre un hábito terminado en el pasado (*went... three years ago*) y una situación que continúa en el presente (*has been... for the last six months*).

questions.statement:
"You look much better! ________ you ________ more water lately?"
"Yes, I ________ a liter of water before breakfast this morning."
questions.context: A doctor talking to a patient about recent habits.

options.feedback: Correct! Present Perfect Continuous for a recent habit (*lately*) and Past Simple for a specific past time (*this morning*).
Incorrect. "Lately" is a marker for Present Perfect.
Incorrect. "This morning" is considered a finished time in this context.
Incorrect. Improper use of tenses for recent and specific past actions.

questions.explanation:
*Lately* indica una tendencia reciente (Presente Perfecto Continuo), mientras que una acción completada en un momento específico de hoy (*this morning*) se expresa habitualmente en *Past Simple*.

questions.statement: Bogotá's Ciclovía ________ in 1974, and it ________ a Sunday tradition for millions of people ever since.
questions.context: Discussing the popularity of "Ciclovía" in Bogotá.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The start date is a specific past point.
Incorrect. The second part needs to show the tradition continues.
Correct! Specific start date in the past and a state that continues to the present.
Incorrect. The year 1974 requires Past Simple.

questions.explanation:
El evento histórico del inicio de la Ciclovía se narra en *Past Simple*. El hecho de que siga siendo una tradición se expresa con *Present Perfect* acompañado de *ever since*.

questions.statement: Which sentence implies that the person **still** lives a healthy life?

options.text: I was very healthy when I was a teenager.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This only refers to the past.

options.text: I lived a healthy life for ten years.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This implies the ten-year period is finished.

options.text: I have lived a healthy life for ten years.
options.feedback: Correct! Present Perfect implies the state started ten years ago and continues now.

options.text: I have been healthy last month.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Last month" is a finished time, so Present Perfect shouldn't be used.

questions.explanation:
El uso de *for* con el *Present Perfect* indica la duración de una acción o estado que aún es válido en el presente. Si usáramos *Past Simple*, la acción se consideraría terminada.

questions.statement:
"I **have seen** (1) a nutritionist **yesterday** (2) because I **wanted** (3) to change my eating habits. I **haven't eaten** (4) junk food since then."

Which part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect?
questions.context: Correcting a common error in a conversation about diet.

options.feedback: Correct! With "yesterday", you must use Past Simple: "I saw".
Incorrect. "Yesterday" is a correct time marker for the past.
Incorrect. Past Simple is correct here for a past intention.
Incorrect. Present Perfect is correct with "since then".

questions.explanation:
Un error común en el nivel B2 es mezclar el *Present Perfect* con marcadores de tiempo terminado como *yesterday*. En esos casos, el *Past Simple* es obligatorio.

questions.statement: Since the government ________ the tax on sugary drinks, the consumption of soda ________ significantly.
questions.context: Discussing the impact of sugar taxes.

options.feedback: Correct! The introduction was a specific past event, and the fall is an ongoing result.
Incorrect. Improper sequence of tenses.
Incorrect. Doesn't emphasize the current result.

questions.explanation:

questions.statement:
Read the following sentence:
"The rate of childhood obesity **increased** (A) between 2010 and 2020, but recent studies **showed** (B) that it **has stabilized** (C) since local schools **started** (D) promoting better nutrition."

Which verb is used incorrectly in the context of a current report?
questions.context: Evaluating the use of tenses in a health report.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is correct for a finished time period (2010-2020).
Incorrect. "Show" should be in Present Perfect (*have shown*) to indicate the relevance of recent studies to the present.
Incorrect. Present Perfect is correct with *since*.
Incorrect. Past Simple is correct after *since* to mark the starting point.

questions.explanation:
Para reportar hallazgos de estudios recientes que tienen validez actual, el *Present Perfect* es más apropiado que el *Past Simple*, ya que conecta los resultados con el presente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"I've just finished my workout."
What does this sentence tell us about the speaker?

options.text: They finished their workout a long time ago.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Just" implies a very recent completion.

options.text: They are likely still tired or at the gym.
options.feedback: Correct! "Just" with Present Perfect shows an action finished moments ago with present consequences.

options.text: They finish their workout at the same time every day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is not about a routine.

options.text: They didn't finish the workout properly.
options.feedback: Incorrect. It only refers to the timing.

questions.explanation:
El uso de *just* con el *Present Perfect* enfatiza que la acción se completó hace un instante, lo cual suele implicar un estado presente (como estar sudado o cansado tras el ejercicio).

questions.statement:
Choose the best summary for a blog post that uses both tenses correctly:
"I ________ a professional athlete for five years before I ________ a knee injury in 2018. Since then, I ________ my focus to coaching and healthy living."

options.text: have been / have had / have shifted
options.feedback: Incorrect. The first two parts are finished past events.
Incorrect. The third part continues to the present.
Correct! Past Simple for the finished career and injury, Present Perfect for the current focus.
Incorrect. Inconsistent use of tenses.

questions.explanation: Este ejercicio requiere evaluar la línea de tiempo completa: hechos pasados terminados (*was/had*) frente a una nueva dirección que se mantiene hasta hoy (*have shifted*).
